source.title: [Paper] All's Fair In Love And Love: Copy Suppression in GPT-2 Small
source.authors: CallumMcDougall; Arthur Conmy; Tom McGrath; Neel Nanda

page_placements.theme: Refinements and look-alikes of the copy-suppression mechanism

record.file_problem: The complete post is present, but it is an accompanying summary of the linked paper, not the full paper itself.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports results from the original study's copy-suppression-preserving ablation and related measurements for GPT-2 Small. It summarizes the original method rather than reporting a separate reproduction.
record.gate_note: Rows record results the post attributes to the authors' own work. Statements about prior work on induction heads and self-repair are not treated as new results; the post's own comparison of anti-induction and copy-suppression scores is included.
record.test_reason: This is the original authors' companion blog post to arXiv:2310.04625, the claim's original source. It restates the paper's results and adds no independent test or new data, so no verdicts are given. It should not count as independent evidence.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also say copy suppression explains only some IOI self-repair. They add that understanding of L10H7's query input is lacking and that larger-model copy suppressors are less clean.
record.recipe_differences: This is an accompanying post summarizing the original study's method and results, not a separate application of a different method.
record.method_sensitivity: The post notes that KL divergence can miss changes to low-probability tokens; it says using fraction of loss recovered alongside KL helped check robustness.

fits_no_version.finding: Copy suppression extends to semantically similar tokens (capitalization, plurals, tense), beyond what embedding cosine similarity predicts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Copy-suppression heads suppress semantically related variants of attended tokens, not only exact copies.

record.peer_reviewed: preprint; the post appeared on Alignment Forum
record.problems: This is a summary rather than the full paper and gives few numerical details beyond 76.9%. The post itself says the account is incomplete, notes limited understanding of L10H7's query input, and discusses a potential limitation of KL divergence.
record.rows_left_out: No further results are reported in enough detail in the post to record separately; references to appendices and the interactive webpage do not supply their underlying results here.

untested.parts: Calibration and overconfidence are not discussed.
There is no distribution-wide decomposition of self-repair sources.

missing.what: Projecting the query-side residual onto unembedding directions significantly harms performance. This means the QK account via unembeddings is incomplete.
missing.locator: Limitations and Future Work (cites Appendix N)

missing.what: Copy suppression explains some but not all IOI self-repair. Unembedding directions did not explain self-repair well.
In larger models, no heads were found as clean as L10H7; copy suppressors there don't just use unembedding directions.

record.verdict_notes: Labels are withheld because the post is the original authors' summary of the original source paper. The record's 'tests/T1' guess should be reclassified so that this post is not double-counted as a replication.

versions.untested_parts: The post states that L10H7 performs copy suppression across the whole distribution, but provides limited numerical detail about the distribution-level result.
The post reports 76.9% performance recovery and describes CSPA, but does not provide detailed separate tests of the QK and OV circuits.
Calibration and overconfidence are not tested.
The self-repair discussion is a qualitative case study on the IOI task, not a measurement across the training distribution.
The post reports an anti-induction/copy-suppression score correlation and mentions L11H10, but does not establish the same role across other model sizes or models.
The post does not test whether self-repair across the distribution mainly comes from other mechanisms.

rows.value: L11H10 performs copy suppression to a lesser extent.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Compared anti-induction scores with copy-suppression scores.

conditions.value: quadrant where both scores are positive

rows.measure: Correlation between anti-induction scores and copy-suppression scores
rows.value: Strong correlation in the quadrant where both scores were positive.
rows.note: The copy-suppression score is described as measuring how much the indirect-object token is suppressed in the IOI task.
rows.check: Original source's result. The correlation holds only in the positive-positive quadrant, and no coefficient is given.

source_check.problem: The prose states the correlation and score conditions, but the missing graph prevents verification that the comparison is restricted to GPT2-Small.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Ablated copying components in the IOI self-repair case study.

rows.baseline: Copying components not ablated; quantitative baseline not stated
rows.value: The post states that when copying is ablated, there is nothing to copy-suppress, producing self-repair.
rows.note: The post does not identify the model or report a numerical size for this effect.
rows.check: The subject is GPT-2 small (IOI case study), not 'not stated'. The post says copy suppression explains 'some, but not all' of IOI self-repair, so partial attribution should be noted. This is an original-source result.
